column6: The object `<sub>/contenders/<name>/<box>`: `{name, state: refused | nameless | waiting, box, hostname, server, instance, holder, holder_box, since, at}`; `refused` \u2014 NameOnAnotherBox by the capture table of N3 \u00abcapture\u00bb, including an occupied unreleased lapsed row of another box; `nameless` \u2014 its own former capture is gone, the worker waits; `waiting` \u2014 it has had no capture of its own yet, and there is no candidate without NameOnAnotherBox. The priority of refused is above the other two. On a decommissioned server (N3 \u00abstart()\u00bb step 3) there is no mark: the worker is nobody without a name search and is not a contender. In a search without a given name `name` is `-` and `holder` is `\\"`; with a given name \u2014 the sought name and its current holder. column6: ([domain key set contract](../../common/contracts/keys.md) \u00ab\u041e\u0442\u0437\u044b\u0432\u044b\u00bb). Two identical requests \u2014 two tokens; no memory of the issued ones is needed, except for a kind with `keep: true`: the row `domain/issued` (P/08.2 N1.6a). On a refusal `revoked` to a token of such a kind the worker requests a new one with the word `revoked: <jti of this token>` (the local door contract), otherwise a circle of refusals for years. An answer with the same `jti` (the word is not executed: `REVOKED_WORDS`, the row `domain/revoked` at 80 %, P/08.2 N1.6a) \u2014 the worker does not request again until the end of the day by its own clock, the log: the rule is common for a worker of any kind with `keep`, otherwise a worker outside `cam`, `rec` goes into the circle request \u2192 the same token \u2192 `revoked` (ADR-0110 addendum (23) item 2).
